name: § 1, point i – 63
title: REPORT on a European Parliament recommendation to the Council, the Commission and the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy concerning EU-China political relations
part_text: i) ensure that the EU’s de-risking strategy is accompanied by climate, energy and industrial policies that avoid increasing dependencies on Chinese components and technologies as well as targeted investment in European industrial capacity and innovation, particularly in critical technologies and advanced materials, to reduce external dependencies, move production to the EU and foster competitiveness within the single market; in particular, de-risking must prioritise strategic autonomy, sustainability, and circular-economy solutions that fully comply with human rights, indigenous rights, and environmental standards; guarantee, however, that measures aimed at reducing strategic dependencies do not impose disproportionate costs on European industry, small and medium-sized enterprises, workers and consumers or undermine Member States’ international competitiveness; insist that de-risking must be targeted, proportionate and based on demonstrable security risks rather than serving as a justification for broad economic decoupling from China;
